_comment: Deploy targets for this site (web-builder-skills:website-deployment).
Consumed by deploy.mjs - run it with `npm run deploy`.
LIVE. quickeasysoftware.com and www are served by the CloudFront distribution below,
from a private OAC-only bucket. The old WordPress distribution E2RXDDD1LJ0WFC in
account 673190877114 is disabled and no longer holds the aliases; its origin
mywebsite.quickeasysoftware.com is still up and is both the rollback target
(infra/rollback.mjs) and the origin for the /wp-content/* behaviour. Do not delete it.
The zone lives in a second account. Assume the cross-account role to touch it:
aws --profile qes-dns route53 ...
Records NOT to touch: MX, SPF, the three DKIM selector groups (google._domainkey,
k2/k3 for Mailchimp, and eight random-selector SES CNAMEs), _dmarc, _amazonses,
and every bos*/dev*/portal/app/docs/mail/login/lambda host.
deploy.mjs invalidates /* on every deploy, which is what makes a long immutable
TTL safe despite unhashed filenames — the invalidation, not the header, is what
forces a re-fetch. If the distribution ever goes away, drop css/js back to a short
revalidating value or a CSS fix will be invisible to returning visitors.
Also covers the generated /pagefind/ search bundle. Its index chunks carry
content hashes, but pagefind.js and pagefind-entry.json do not, so they stay
on the short page TTL rather than an immutable one — the per-deploy /*
invalidation is what makes a rebuilt index visible immediately.

notes: The exclude list keeps dev artifacts off the public endpoint. Note that adding an
--exclude does NOT remove a file already in the bucket: sync applies filters to the
destination too, so --delete skips excluded keys. Anything already published has to
be removed with an explicit `aws s3 rm <key>`.
The bucket is private: Block Public Access fully on, BucketOwnerEnforced, no website
hosting, readable only by this distribution via OAC. There is no S3 website endpoint
A /wp-content/* cache behaviour points at the WordPress origin with the AllViewer
origin request policy, so indexed image URLs and third-party hot-links keep working
after the cutover. Remove it once Search Console stops reporting hits, and note it
depends on mywebsite.quickeasysoftware.com continuing to resolve.
